dx: Hemiballismus secondary to acute lacunar infarct of the left subthalamic nucleus
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Hemiballismus secondary to acute lacunar infarct of the left subthalamic nucleus

This presentation is classic: sudden-onset, continuous, large-amplitude flinging/throwing movements of the right leg. The flinging quality (rather than twisting or curling), unilateral involvement, and sudden onset are hallmarks of hemiballismus. The most common cause is a small vessel ischemic stroke (lacunar infarct) affecting the contralateral subthalamic nucleus, which fits this patient's presentation. Brain MRI with DWI would confirm an acute infarct in the left subthalamic region.
